2887.unvetted: Leaf not seen. The volume is digitised, but only on Orient-Digital, which resets the connection from this network (as does Qalamos). Correct shelfmark: SBB Wetzstein II 203, not Wetzstein I 203. Ahlwardt's 'We.' is Wetzstein II, and K10plus PPN 1982423900 / Qalamos DE1Book_manuscript_00022629 give 'Wetzstein II 203', Diwan of ad-Darwish Mustafa al-Hazayini as-Sukkari, 1117 [1705], 145 Bl., digitised 2026 in 'Islamische Handschriften digital', Public Domain. Its resolver (SBB00048A9700000000) answers NOTFOUND on digital.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de, there is no METS on content.staatsbibliothek-berlin.de, and the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek has a bot check (Anubis), which was not passed. Ahlwardt vol. 1 no. 13 note 1 (cipher 'an einigen Stellen', key on f. 103a) and no. 8012 (vol. 7) were read on archive.org: no folios for the cipher passages, no reading. known.py, DECODE ('Wetzstein', 'Sukkari') and a web search found nothing. Next: open the Orient-Digital/Qalamos copy from another network, find the cipher passages and f. 103a, and test the key.

2888.unvetted: Not established as cipher, and the leaf itself was not seen. Sellheim, VOHD XVII A 2 (1987), Tafel 22 Abb. 37 (SBB digital PPN1879940027, image 462, 2184 x 3171 px; the strip is about 990 x 240 px at full size) shows one underlined line of about 16 signs to the left of the 'ya kabikaj' invocation. They are groups of 2, 3 and 4 upright strokes, some crossed or joined at the top, two looped signs and a hooked sign. That looks like a stroke-group numeral notation (a rumi/Fasi- or zimam-type numeral sequence) as much as a cipher. The signs do not match the Greek-Coptic foliation numerals on Sellheim's Tafel 24 Abb. 46-47. Sellheim's own entry (printed p. 66, image 94, not p. 65) says 'daneben Geheimschrift (?; s. Abb. 37)' and gives no reading. His caption reads '37. Geheimschrift, nach 917/1511 (s. S. 66 u. Abb. 10, 34)', tying the hand to the scribe's siglum and to al-Gharbi's colophon. Ms. or. oct. 1474 is not found in the K10plus SBB catalogue by shelfmark, and Qalamos/Orient-Digital are unreachable here. Next: see f. 1a at full size, compare the signs with rumi/Fasi and zimam numeral tables, and decide numerals or not_cipher.

2893.unvetted: Leaf not seen, and the description does not show that it is a cipher. Savage-Smith, New Catalogue of Arabic MSS in the Bodleian I: Medicine (2011), entry 8, as given in the Fihrist TEI (manuscript_11359), says only: 'On folio 101a, between two sections of text, there are some curious letter forms and undeciphered writing'. That could equally be pen trials, another script or charakteres. Both Digital Bodleian objects were checked through their IIIF manifests: bcc68154-303d-43cb-bee6-c5ddffcd8d39 has 3 canvases (fol. 1a, 1b-2a, 170a), and eacd31dd-5101-4cde-8e89-f285f3bb85d2 has 1 canvas (fol. 001v-002r). Neither shows f. 101a. Web searches on the shelfmark found no study of the passage, and known.py and DECODE ('Laud Or', 'Bodleian Arabic') found nothing. Next: an image order for f. 101a from the Bodleian, or a reading-room visit, then decide.

2894.key_check: No key has been tested; the inscription has not been seen. The candidate systems are a substitution of Arabic letters by abjad numeral values written in mixed Arabic and Coptic (zimam) numerals, and the Coptic scribal cryptography keyed in the two sibling sources below.
2894.key_held: Untested. Two possible keys from the same Coptic scribal milieu, both listed in the Arabic sweep part C: BnF Arabe 238 f. 384v, 'Clef d'un chiffre dont se servaient les écrivains coptes' (de Slane; Gallica btv1b11004021j, not opened), and Vat. ar. 28 (1271), where 'alia manus clavem cryptogrammatis addidit' (BAV record 116992; digitised, not opened).
